data.narrative:
Peak Energy, founded by Landon Mossburg and Liam O'Connor, is a Series A climate and energy company that has raised $65M to date. The Climate & Energy sector encompasses a competitive peer universe of 9 private companies and 1 public comparable (Lanza Tech, ticker LNZA), though peers include later-stage ventures like Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen.

Given the absence of sufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the sector—only 0 peers met narrow-filter criteria—the peer-median valuation method is not applicable. Instead, the analysis relies on stage-progression methodology, which applies a typical Series A-to-next-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x to the $65M total raised proxy, implying a post-money valuation of $130M. This method reflects observed financing dynamics as capital moves from seed to later institutional rounds.

The triangulated valuation range supported by available methods is $110M to $150M, with a median point of $130M. The analysis reflects material uncertainty given the single-method reliance and the absence of tight peer valuation data at Peak Energy's stage. Key drivers of ultimate valuation will include technology maturity, revenue traction, and capital efficiency relative to the broader Climate & Energy venture cohort.
